correctness.rationale: A smooth quartic has surjective degree-ten ideal map exactly when its homogeneous Jacobian ideal is projectively empty: the degree-four basepoint-free linear subsystem contains a regular sequence of three quartics, with quotient socle degree nine. The exact 32767-mask Macaulay elimination finds 10920 smooth forms; the three-to-one counting of 17390184 eligible smooth unordered pairs gives 5796728 pencils. Exact seven-point intersection gives the base distribution, which is independently reproduced by full Walsh-transform subset inversion. Burnside fixed counts and order-21 normalizer test yield 34539 orbits and four exact stabilizer sizes. Full positive projective-orbit smoothness is independently checked by 234 affine Groebner unit-ideal tests; negative completeness depends on the exhaustive original elimination, not an unsupported finite sample.

value.rationale: The exact complete finite-field census refines the motivated published smooth-pencil existence problem in the first nontrivial positive-genus plane-quartic degree over the smallest field. It determines how every rational-base configuration contributes and exhausts rational projective orbit stabilizers; those constraints are neither a routine restatement of the existing individual-curve census nor implied by general existence. The lone eight-element plane-filling orbit is one strict special family, highlighting meaningful scope beyond the previously computed special case.
